_comment: Committed catalogue of containment actions IANUA may PLAN. Every entry is restrict-only (it reduces an adversary's capability; nothing here grants access, moves laterally, or modifies a third party), carries an explicit rollback, and names its execution owner. IANUA never executes any of these — agents/response/ emits a draft plan a human carries out, and tests/security/test_response_no_executor.py fails the build if executor code ever appears. See DESIGN.md 5 boundary 8.

actions.title: Capture volatile memory and process state before any disruption
actions.rationale: Killing a process destroys its volatile memory — often the only copy of injected code, decrypted configuration, and C2 keys. Evidence capture therefore precedes every disruptive tier, without exception.
steps: Acquire a memory image of the affected host using the team's approved tooling.
Record the full process tree with parent linkage, command lines, and open handles.
Hash and store the acquisition alongside the incident record.
actions.rollback: None required — collection is non-destructive and read-only.

actions.title: Preserve and forward host log evidence
actions.rationale: Where the incident involves evidence destruction or sensor tampering, the surviving copies live off-host. Securing them early bounds what the adversary can still erase.
steps: Export the relevant window from the central log platform and store it read-only.
Verify whether forwarding was interrupted, and record any gap explicitly.
actions.rollback: None required — collection is non-destructive and read-only.

actions.title: Revoke active sessions and refresh tokens for the affected account
actions.rationale: Session revocation removes an adversary's current access without deleting the account or its history, and the user can simply sign in again — the highest-value reversible containment available for credential compromise.
steps: Revoke active sessions and refresh tokens for the account in the identity provider.
Require re-authentication with a second factor on next sign-in.
Record the revocation time so subsequent activity is unambiguously post-containment.
actions.rollback: None needed — the legitimate user re-authenticates normally.

actions.title: Place the host in network isolation, retaining management access
actions.rationale: Isolation severs command-and-control and lateral movement while leaving the host running — memory, processes, and on-disk artefacts stay available for analysis, which powering off would destroy.
steps: Move the host to the quarantine segment, retaining the analyst management path.
Confirm the isolation took effect and note any sessions that survived it.
Record the service impact so the business owner can weigh restoration timing.
actions.rollback: Return the host to its production segment once analysis concludes and the compromise is remediated.

actions.title: Block egress to a corroborated malicious destination
actions.rationale: Blocking a destination is cheap and reversible, but it is also the action a poisoned feed would most like to trigger. Only corroborated, non-never-flagged indicators are ever proposed, and the block is scoped and time-boxed.
steps: Confirm the destination is corroborated by independent sources and outside all never-flag ranges.
Apply a scoped, time-boxed egress block and log the change with its expiry.
Watch for the affected host retrying the destination, which confirms the implant is still active.
actions.rollback: Remove the block entry; it is time-boxed and expires on its own if missed.

actions.title: Reset credentials for the affected account
actions.rationale: Credential reset ends persistent access but cannot be undone and disrupts the legitimate user. AGENTS.md 5.1 assigns secret handling to a human without exception: no agent in this platform reads, stores, or rotates a credential.
steps: A human administrator resets the credential through the identity provider directly.
Verify the reset out-of-band with the account owner before restoring access.
Audit for attacker-installed persistence that survives a password change: SSH authorized keys, API tokens, OAuth grants, mail forwarding rules.
actions.rollback: Not reversible. The account owner regains access through the standard credential-recovery process.

actions.title: Quarantine a suspect file after acquisition
actions.rationale: Quarantine removes the payload from its execution path. It is listed as evidence-affecting because moving a file alters timestamps and can trip attacker tripwires; acquisition of a forensic copy comes first.
steps: Acquire and hash a forensic copy before touching the original.
Move the file to the quarantine store with its original path and metadata recorded.
Confirm nothing legitimate depended on the path before it is left absent.
actions.rollback: Restore the file from quarantine to its recorded original path.

actions.title: Terminate a confirmed malicious process
actions.rationale: Termination stops active harm but irreversibly destroys the process's volatile memory — frequently the only place the implant is unpacked and its configuration readable. Memory capture is a hard prerequisite, and a wrong identification here is a self-inflicted outage on a production service.
steps: Verify the process identity against the acquired process tree, not the alert alone.
Confirm the memory capture completed and is readable before proceeding.
Terminate the process and record whether it respawned, which indicates persistence.
actions.rollback: Not reversible. If the identification was wrong, restart the legitimate service from its normal management path and record the outage.
